candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — cervical cancer screening / preventive care
candidate.educational_objective: Apply current cervical cancer screening guidance by recognizing a 5-year interval for hrHPV/cytology co-testing in average-risk clients age 30 to 65 when co-testing is selected.
candidate.rationale: ACOG's 2026 cervical cancer screening guidance states that co-testing with high-risk HPV testing and cervical cytology every 5 years is acceptable for average-risk individuals age 30 to 65 when primary hrHPV testing is not available or, after counseling, the patient chooses co-testing. Therefore C is correct. Annual or 2-year co-testing is more frequent than the recommended interval, and a single lifetime screen is inadequate.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For average-risk individuals age 30–65, hrHPV/cytology co-testing every 5 years is an acceptable screening strategy under the conditions stated by ACOG's 2026 guidance.
candidate.source_locator: Summary recommendations/Table 1: co-testing with hrHPV and cervical cytology every 5 years for individuals aged 30–65 years is acceptable when primary hrHPV testing is not available or the patient chooses co-testing after counseling
candidate.source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)
candidate.stem: An average-risk client age 30 to 65 chooses cervical cancer screening with high-risk HPV testing plus cervical cytology (co-testing) after counseling. According to current ACOG guidance, which screening interval is acceptable?
